claim: Claude Code dominates at small companies (75% usage), GitHub Copilot at enterprises (56%), based on 900+ developer survey
quote: 95% of surveyed engineers use AI tools weekly or more. 56% complete 70%+ of their engineering work with AI.

claim: GitHub Copilot pricing: Free ($0, 2k completions/mo), Pro ($10/mo), Pro+ ($39/mo), Max ($100/mo)
quote: Free: $0/month with 2,000 completions per month. Pro: $10/month with unlimited completions.

claim: GitHub Copilot /tests slash command scaffolds a full test suite from the open file, detecting existing test conventions
quote: You can prompt Copilot to write a full suite of unit tests with the /tests slash command, and Copilot will generate unit tests when you have the file open on the current tab of your IDE.

claim: VS Code Copilot supports custom TDD agents (TDD-red, TDD-green, TDD-refactor) with automated phase handoffs via .github/agents/ files
quote: Create separate .github/agents/ files for each TDD phase. Handoffs provide control points where you can assess each step before moving to the next phase.

claim: Cursor pricing: Free (limited), Pro $20/mo, Business $40/user/mo; annual billing saves 20%
quote: Cursor offers a Free tier with limited completions and slow requests, Pro at $20/month, and Business at $40/user/month.

claim: Cursor YOLO mode auto-runs tests, reads failures, and iterates; TDD is more necessary not less when using AI coding tools
quote: Tools like Cursor, Codex, and Copilot are becoming increasingly integrated into developers' daily workflows — TDD is needed to prevent AI from cheating by modifying tests.

claim: Two-session TDD pattern: Phase 1 writes only failing tests with 'DO NOT write the implementation'; Phase 2 implements with 'DO NOT modify the test file'; fresh chat between phases prevents cheating
quote: Write ONLY test cases for a calculateShipping function. DO NOT write the implementation. … Write the implementation for calculateShipping that passes ALL tests in the test file. DO NOT modify the test file.

claim: Continue.dev is an open-source VS Code/JetBrains agent supporting bring-your-own model (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama) with shared version-controlled config
quote: Continue runs source-controlled AI checks on every pull request, and supports shared configuration via version-controlled config files.

claim: Cline is an autonomous VS Code agent that runs dev servers and test commands in the terminal, reads failures, and iterates across files; Plan Mode narrates intent before acting
quote: Cline is an autonomous coding agent that works as a VS Code extension, designed to handle complex, multi-step coding tasks. It handles long-running dev servers, tests, and deploys live.

claim: Aider is a terminal-based, git-native AI coding agent that auto-commits on green test runs, making the TDD loop visible in git history
quote: Aider is purpose-built for terminal-based backend development and integrates with git natively.

claim: Vitest is 2-5x faster than Jest on cold start; watch mode reruns in under 300ms vs Jest's 3-10s; Jest-compatible API enables smooth migrations
quote: Vitest typically starts 2-5x faster than Jest on medium to large codebases. In watch mode, Vitest delivers near-instantaneous file change detection, while Jest's response is noticeably slower.

claim: Vitest is the recommended TypeScript unit testing framework for new projects in 2026
quote: Vitest uses esbuild to transform TypeScript, which is dramatically faster and more reliable.

claim: Jest remains the industry-proven alternative for existing JavaScript/TypeScript codebases
quote: Jest is an industry-proven testing framework since 2014 with widespread adoption.

claim: Playwright is the recommended browser/E2E testing framework; AI tools generate Playwright selectors natively and its codegen command records tests from browser interactions
quote: Multi-browser support across Chromium, Firefox, WebKit. Built-in debugging, screenshots, and video recording.

claim: GitHub Codespaces provides one-click workshop environments via devcontainer; broken environments can be recreated in 2 minutes
quote: A fresh development environment is a case of clicking a button and then waiting for a couple of minutes, and if you break it, you can click the button again to get a new one.

claim: NICAR 2026 coding-agents workshop used Codespaces + devcontainer with YOLO-mode aliases pre-wired so participants skipped all permission dialogs
quote: 'claude-yolo' and 'codex-yolo' aliases for running agents without asking for permission for every action — used safely within containerized Codespaces.

claim: Qodo v2.0 multi-agent PR review architecture achieved 60.1% F1 score, 9 points ahead of next best tool; test generation analyzes behavioral specs not just code paths
quote: This architecture achieved the highest overall F1 score of 60.1% in comparative benchmarks against seven other leading AI code review tools, outperforming the next best solution by 9%.

claim: Qodo pricing: Free (250 credits/mo, 30 PR reviews), Teams $30-38/user/mo
quote: Free tier includes 75 PRs + 250 credits/month. Teams plan costs $30-38/user/month.

claim: Mutation testing exposes that AI-generated tests are oracle-designed to pass rather than catch bugs; fast unit tests and version control (commit on green, revert on red) are essential with AI tools
quote: The more things we ask models to pay attention to, the less able they are to pay attention to any of them. Testing after each small change prevents broken code from polluting the model's context.

claim: mutmut is a Python mutation testing tool that runs pytest on the test suite after applying code mutations to reveal tests that pass but fail to catch bugs
quote: Mutmut runs pytest on tests in the tests or test folder and tries to figure out where the code to mutate is.
